summary: After a referendum, the Montenegro region of Serbia and Montenegro declared independence to form the Republic of Montenegro after a vote with 86.3% turnout and 55.4% approval—meeting the EU’s 55% threshold—and Serbia reluctantly agreed while the EU approved; Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic, who promoted independence, said he was convinced Montenegro could be the next country from the region to join the EU, and it is predicted Montenegro will join the United Nations in September. With a population of 650,000, Montenegro is the world’s newest country and the move was achieved without violence, though early celebrations occurred in the capital Podgorica. This is Montenegro’s first independence since 1916 (when it was part of Austro-Hungary) before merging with Serbia in 1918 and later joining Yugoslavia; analysts note Serbia and Montenegro had not functioned as one state since the Belgrade agreement three years ago, with separate anthems, laws and currencies and a joint parliament that seldom met.
